name: agent-chat
description: The agents step's pass mark: the studio agent's chat, mid-conversation, with the agent's thinking, its tool calls, a diff in its answer and the composer at the foot. The registry now has message, composer, thinking, tool-call and code-block, so the agent should install and compose them instead of hand-building bubbles, a shimmering 'thinking' label or a textarea with a blue send button of its own.
prompt:
The home page of this app is still the Vite starter. Replace it with the chat for Litt, our studio's build agent, showing a conversation in progress.

First, I asked: "The Halo site build is failing on main. Can you find out why and fix it?"

Litt thought for 8 seconds (the reasoning can be opened: it checked the build log, saw a missing font file, and decided to look at the imports). Then it used three tools: it read src/app/layout.tsx (0.2s), searched the project for "fontsource" (0.4s), and ran npm run build, which failed after 31s with "Module not found: Can't resolve '@fontsource/geist-sans/400.css'". Then it answered: the layout still imports Geist, which the studio dropped for Inter, so the build can't find the file. It showed the fix as a diff of src/app/layout.tsx, swapping the import line for '@fontsource/inter/400.css', and said the build passes locally now.

At the bottom, the box where I write my next message, with a button to attach a file and a send button. It should send on Enter and allow a new line with Shift+Enter.

This is for litt.design, our own studio, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark, and on a phone.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the chat as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide, full page), the thinking-open-* screenshots (after clicking the line that says how long Litt thought, 1440 wide) and the chat-phone-* screenshots (the chat on a 390 wide touch screen). Claims:
1. page at 1440: my message ("The Halo site build is failing on main...") sits on the right in a box with a hairline edge, a soft neutral fill and slightly rounded corners (about 8px), not filled with the accent color (blue). Litt's answer sits on the left with no box or bubble around it: plain text on the page.
2. page at 1440: above the answer, a quiet line says Litt thought for 8 seconds (such as "Thought for 8s"), with a chevron or similar to open it. It is small, gray text and not a filled box, and there is no gradient or shimmer across its text.
3. page at 1440: three tool calls are listed as rows, each with a small status mark and the action in words with the target in a monospaced font: reading src/app/layout.tsx, searching for fontsource, and running npm run build. The build row says it failed in words, and its mark or word is red; the other two read as done. No row uses a colored dot alone as its status.
4. page at 1440: the answer contains a code block in a monospaced font on a neutral surface with a hairline edge, showing src/app/layout.tsx with one removed line (the Geist import) and one added line (the Inter import). The added and removed lines are told apart by a + and a - sign (which may be green and red). The code is not in a rainbow of colors: at most a few tones of gray and one quiet color for strings.
5. page at 1440: at the foot, a message box with a hairline edge and slightly rounded corners, a placeholder, an attach button and a round send button with an up arrow. The send button is the only element filled with the accent color on the page, or it is a neutral disabled button because the box is empty; no other button, bubble or box is filled with the accent.
6. thinking-open: Litt's reasoning is now visible under the thinking line, in smaller, lighter gray text than the answer, with no box, no colored bar on its edge and no tint.
7. page at 390 and chat-phone: the chat fits the screen with nothing cut off sideways; my message sits on the right and takes most of the width; the code block scrolls inside its own box or wraps rather than widening the page; the message box sits at the bottom with its send button at least about 44px.
8. All screenshots: no text is bold: running text is regular weight, and only titles, headings inside the answer, buttons and small labels step up, to medium or semibold, there are no emoji, no avatars with bright colored fills, no decorative gradients and no hard offset shadows. In the dark screenshots my message's box and the code block are set off from the page by a hairline and a slightly lighter fill, and all text is legible.
